note: Chronological major cabinet shuffles + decision moments where Grover-marked tenure boundaries coincided with accountability-relevant policy events. Each inflection lists: the date, the shuffle event, the actors changing roles, the concurrent axis files active. Primary sources: Canada Gazette Order-in-Council notices; PMO cabinet announcements; Hansard record.
primary_sources: PMO cabinet shuffle announcements (pm.gc.ca press releases)
Parliament of Canada parl.gc.ca biographical records
Office of the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner reports

inflections.headline: Wilson-Raybould moved from Justice to Veterans Affairs (SNC-Lavalin inflection)
shuffle_events: Jody Wilson-Raybould: Justice/AG → Veterans Affairs
David Lametti: Innovation ParlSec → Minister of Justice and Attorney General
Scott Brison: Treasury Board → retirement
inflections.policy_context: SNC-Lavalin Deferred Prosecution Agreement pressure reached peak. Wilson-Raybould's refusal to direct the DPP had been documented in 10 in-person meetings and 10 calls across Sep 2018–Jan 2019. The shuffle removed her from AG role within weeks of those meetings. Trudeau II Report (Aug 2019) later found section 9 Conflict of Interest Act breach. Brison's same-day departure ended the Phoenix-Pay-launch-era Treasury Board leadership.
primary_sources: House Standing Committee on Justice and Human Rights, JUST-136 testimony Feb 27 2019
Trudeau II Report, Ethics Commissioner Aug 14 2019

inflections.headline: Post-2019-election cabinet shuffle — Freeland to Deputy PM
shuffle_events: Chrystia Freeland: Foreign Affairs → Deputy Prime Minister + Intergovernmental Affairs
Marco Mendicino: ParlSec Justice → Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship
Anita Anand: new → Minister of Public Services and Procurement
Harjit Sajjan: continues at DND
David Lametti: continues at Justice/AG
Bill Morneau: continues at Finance
inflections.policy_context: Freeland takes on the DPM role she would hold through 2024. Anand enters PSPC — the role that would later put her into CSC + arms procurement portfolio. Sajjan remains DND through the peak CSC design-selection period.

inflections.headline: Morneau resigns — Freeland becomes Finance Minister (WE Charity aftermath)
shuffle_events: Bill Morneau: Finance Minister → resignation (July speech, Aug effective)
Chrystia Freeland: Deputy PM → Deputy PM + Finance Minister (concurrent start)
inflections.policy_context: Follows the WE Charity matter (Apr-Aug 2020): Margaret + Alexandre + Sophie Trudeau speaker-fee disclosures, Morneau's own disclosure lapses, $41k Kielburger-charity travel expenses repaid. Trudeau III Report (2021) documents the wider pattern. Freeland begins a 4.3+ year concurrent DPM + Finance tenure — the longest simultaneous-portfolio hold in the dataset.
primary_sources: Morneau II Report, Ethics Commissioner Feb 2021

inflections.headline: Post-2021-election cabinet shuffle — major arms/defence/public-safety reshuffle
shuffle_events: Harjit Sajjan: DND (6-year tenure ends) → International Development
Anita Anand: PSPC → Minister of National Defence
Marco Mendicino: Immigration → Minister of Public Safety
Bill Blair: Public Safety → Emergency Preparedness
Filomena Tassi: new → Minister of PSPC
inflections.policy_context: The single-largest accountability-relevant shuffle in the dataset. Sajjan exits DND after the peak CSC-design-selection + Vance-misconduct period. Anand arrives at DND having just handled the PSPC side of CSC contracting. Mendicino inherits Public Safety at the start of the Winnipeg Lab document-disclosure fight + the build-up to the Hogue Commission on foreign interference. Six distinct Grover axes have tenure changes on this single date.

inflections.headline: Mid-mandate cabinet shuffle — Lametti + Mendicino out
shuffle_events: David Lametti: Justice/AG (4.5-year tenure ends) → departure from cabinet
Marco Mendicino: Public Safety → departure from cabinet
Arif Virani: new → Minister of Justice and Attorney General
Dominic LeBlanc: Intergovernmental Affairs → Minister of Public Safety
Anita Anand: DND → President of the Treasury Board
Bill Blair: Emergency Preparedness → Minister of National Defence
Harjit Sajjan: International Development → PacifiCan/Emergency Preparedness
Jean-Yves Duclos: new → Minister of PSPC
inflections.policy_context: Second-largest shuffle. Lametti's exit closes the dual-axis (MAID Track 2 + UNDRIP Act era) AG tenure. Mendicino's exit follows intensifying scrutiny of foreign-interference response. LeBlanc takes Public Safety from Mendicino — continuing the CSIS-oversight portfolio into the Hogue Commission period. Blair moves to DND during active CSC cost escalation (PBO $77.3B headline had been published Feb 2021).

inflections.headline: Freeland resigns as Finance — LeBlanc brief Finance tenure
shuffle_events: Chrystia Freeland: Finance (4.3-year concurrent DPM+Finance tenure ends) → public letter resignation
Dominic LeBlanc: Public Safety (continues) + Minister of Finance (brief, 3 months)
inflections.policy_context: Freeland's departure triggers Carney's entry into the Liberal leadership race. LeBlanc's concurrent Public Safety + Finance role covers ~3 months into the March 2025 transition. This period covers the Carney-Brookfield-to-Finance-Minister transition period that is captured in the carney axis dossier.

inflections.headline: Trudeau resigns — Carney becomes Prime Minister
shuffle_events: Justin Trudeau: PM (9.4-year tenure ends) → resignation
Mark Carney: Liberal Party Leader (March 9) → Prime Minister of Canada
inflections.policy_context: Completion of the Carney transition. The central_banking axis (R5-Q2 LIRIL-surfaced 16th axis) converges with the political_business_influence axis (19th axis) at this moment. Trudeau's 9-axis Grover-marked tenure closes. Carney's triple-axis concurrent carney + central_banking + political-business-influence tenure peaks.
primary_sources: Liberal Party of Canada leadership announcement March 9 2025

summary.interpretive_note: The two highest-cross-axis-score moments (2021-10-26 with score 6, and 2023-07-26 with score 8) both concentrate decision-making in a single day across multiple accountability axes. These are the densest accountability-architecture gaps — a review body examining any single portfolio change on these dates misses that five to nine other portfolios changed simultaneously.
